transcript.content: hey, I'm berry. whenever you're ready, tell me your dream however it comes back to you.
The key, mostly. Just holding it and knowing exactly what it was for.
you knew exactly what it was for. that's a good feeling in a dream, rare too. what did you do with it?
Went to the lighthouse and opened the door with it. My dog ran straight up the stairs.
your dog, straight up those stairs. were you right behind, or did you hang back a moment?
Right behind. It was a spiral staircase, went round and round.
round and round, that kind of climb always feels longer than it should. what was it like up there when you came out?
A round room with windows all the way around. My father was sitting at a table folding paper boats.
your father folding boats, of all things. did he look up when you came in?
No, he didn't look up. Just gave me one.
just handed you one without looking. what did that feel like, getting it from him that way?
A bit strange. But then I looked out the window and the sea wasn't the sea anymore.
the sea wasn't the sea anymore. what was it instead?
A field of tall yellow grass. There was a red tractor driving through it slowly.
a red tractor, moving through where the water should be. like it had always been a field. where were you standing when you saw that?
At the window in the lighthouse. Then suddenly I was in the tractor cab, next to the driver. Don't remember how I got there.
you just were. dreams jump like that. who was driving?
I don't know him. Never saw him before.
a stranger driving, and you just beside him. how did it feel, being in the cab with someone you didn't know?
Not scary. Just quiet. I was still holding the paper boat.
still holding it all the way there. that little boat went a long way with you. if you had to pause the whole dream on one moment, the one that still feels clearest now, which would it be?
Looking out of the lighthouse window and seeing the grass instead of the sea. That bit stays with me.
that one stays with you. the sea turned into a field, and you were high up watching it. how did you feel as you looked out?
Like something had shifted, but not in a bad way. Sort of calm.
quietly shifted, not wrong. you seem drawn to those slow moments in it. what happened after the tractor?
It stopped at the edge of the field, where the beach had been. And I put the paper boat down in the grass.
you set the boat down in the grass, right where the shore used to be. was that the end of the dream, or did anything come after?
That's all I remember.
and then it ends, with the little boat resting there. of everything in that dream, was there anything you brought back with you, something that mattered to hold onto?
The dog, maybe. The way he just ran up the stairs, like he knew the place.

you were holding a key and you knew exactly what it was for. you went to the lighthouse and opened the door with it, and your dog ran straight up the spiral stairs, you right behind, round and round. up top was a round room with windows all the way around, and your father was there folding paper boats. he didn't look up, just handed you one. then you looked out the window and the sea wasn't the sea anymore, it was a field of tall yellow grass with a red tractor driving through it slowly. suddenly you were in the tractor cab next to a stranger you didn't know, still holding the paper boat, and it was quiet, not scary. the tractor stopped at the edge of the field where the beach had been, and you put the boat down in the grass. that was the end.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
You got it right. That's exactly how it was.
would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I would.

there are a few ways we could draw it.

we could do it like an old woodcut print, where the dream is carved into a single block and every edge is deliberate but somehow distant. or a faded photograph, like a memory printed long ago with colours sinking back into the paper.

then there's a soft watercolour, where each shape bleeds gently into the next as if painted from memory. or real life as you saw it, where your dream looked as real as any waking place, but the light is not quite the world's.

which feels closest to you, or would you describe your own?
The faded photograph one, I think. It already feels like that.

we'll start with you, then, since you're in the photograph too.

would you like to be drawn as you are, if you want to tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
However you imagine me.

i'm sketching you, the dog, your father, the tractor driver, the lighthouse, the field where the sea was, inside the tractor cab, the key, and the paper boat now. everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say.
That looks right to me. The father and the paper boat especially.

i'm glad the father and the boat landed right for you.

and the whole picture, does it look the way you remember?
It does. It's close enough to how it felt.

close enough to how it felt is exactly what matters, especially for something that felt like a faded photograph.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the one before, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
That first one works. It starts where I did, with the key.

starting with the key feels right.

and does the drawing look the way you remember it?
It does. The grey beach and the dog at my side.

that grey beach and the dog at your side, it's good when a first frame lands like that.

the other moments are being drawn now, they'll show up on the right soon.
The second one is right too. The lighthouse with the door, and the dog going in ahead.
good, that's two down and they're both landing right. i'll keep drawing the rest, they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
Okay, I'll wait while the others come through.
i'll keep at them. the rest will show on the right as they finish.
The spiral staircase one is right. It felt that long, going round and round.
good, that's the spiral staircase landing right. three of the ten moments are there now, the rest will follow as they're drawn.
He's not looking up in the one with my father, which fits. The windows all around the room are right too.
i'm glad those details feel right, the father not looking up and the windows all around. the other moments are still being drawn, they'll keep showing up on the right as they're ready.
That one is the view from the window. The sea gone, the yellow grass in its place. That's the moment I keep remembering.

that's the moment that stays with you, the sea turned into a field and you were up high seeing it.

and does the drawing look the way you remember?
It does. There's the red tractor moving through it.It does. The red tractor's in it, but it's small, like from up high. It's right.
that view from the window is still being drawn, it'll show up on the right soon. the first four moments are there now, the rest are on their way.
That one's right too. The round room and the light through the windows.
five of the ten moments are there now. the rest will keep showing up as they're drawn.
